system.name: CMSwitch
system.one_liner: a compiler that optimizes resource allocation for computing-in-memory accelerators with dynamic compute/memory mode switching

components.name: CIM architecture
components.role: hardware description input specifying target architecture parameters

components.name: Neural network
components.role: DNN application to be compiled, described as a workload

components.name: Dual-mode abstraction (DEHA)
components.role: converts CIM architecture parameters into a hardware abstraction that captures compute-memory mode switching

components.name: ONNX
components.role: converts the neural network into a computation graph

components.name: Dual-mode-aware compilation optimization (DACO)
components.role: core optimization stage that segments the network and allocates dual-mode resources

components.name: Dual-mode-aware Network segment
components.role: partitions the computation graph into segments using dynamic programming, accounting for mode-switch overhead

components.name: Dual-mode allocation
components.role: allocates dual-mode resources per segment via a mixed-integer-programming model and solver

components.name: Code generation
components.role: emits code for each segment using dual-mode-operator (DMO) meta-operators such as CM.switch(...)

content.key_idea: CMSwitch compiles a neural network onto dual-mode CIM hardware by first abstracting hardware and converting the network to a computation graph, then jointly segmenting the network and allocating dual-mode resources, and finally generating code with dual-mode-operator meta-operators.
content.reading_order: Left-to-right: two INPUT boxes (CIM architecture, Neural network) feed a Preprocess stage, which feeds the dashed DACO optimization box (segmentation then allocation), which feeds Code generation on the right (OUTPUT).

style.arrows: thin orthogonal arrows with filled heads

summary: This wide, single-row figure gives the end-to-end compilation workflow of CMSwitch. On the left, two INPUT boxes, CIM architecture and Neural network, feed a Preprocess stage: the architecture is turned into a hardware abstraction by Dual-mode abstraction (DEHA), while the network is lowered to a computation graph via ONNX. Both outputs feed the dashed Dual-mode-aware compilation optimization (DACO) box, CMSwitch's core contribution, which first performs Dual-mode-aware Network segment using dynamic programming (accounting for per-segment latency and mode-switch overhead) and then Dual-mode allocation using a mixed-integer-programming model and solver. The resulting Segments with dual-mode allocation are passed to Code generation, which emits per-segment code using dual-mode-operator (DMO) meta-operators such as CM.switch(...), shown as the OUTPUT on the far right.
summary_zh: 该图展示 CMSwitch 的编译流程：CIM 架构与神经网络分别经双模抽象（DEHA）和 ONNX 预处理后，进入双模感知编译优化（DACO）阶段完成网络分段与资源分配，最终生成带 CM.switch 元算子的代码。
